reasoning: Two letters on consecutive folded levels align only when their original indices have opposite parity: the fold lies halfway between their indices and must be between letters. Conversely, any increasing sequence of equal letters with alternating index parity is realizable by placing folds at consecutive pairwise midpoints; these fold positions are increasing and each segment contains its selected letter, so the pile starts at the bottom and has no gaps. A two-state longest-subsequence DP per letter therefore computes the exact optimum.
